title: pm-daily-scratchpad-2026-03-05
content:
Morning scratchpad - focus day for hosted API small-launch prep (goal: soft-launch canary tomorrow).

Top priorities
- Finish PRD edits (scope + rollout plan) — need final QA on failure modes section (Priya).
- Lock down canary config + rollback criteria with SRE (Marco).
- Stakeholder updates x2 (PM sync @11:30 + Eng sync @15:00).
- Finalize monitoring dashboards and alert thresholds for latency regressions.

PRD edits (open items)
- Update success metrics: change Live Latency SLO to p95 < 220ms (was 200ms) with caveat re: high seq-len. Add justification paragraph.
- Add explicit compatibility table for deduped models + quantized variants (Sophie to confirm model tags).
- Document fallback policy: route to smaller model + notify client (need wording for API contract).
- Appendix: add test prompts + expected outputs (still rough).
- Acceptance criteria: list of 6 items (traffic tests, regression evals, infra autoscale, logs, alerting, docs).

Stakeholder follow-ups
- Email to Sales Ops (send short note with expected limits + quota default) — draft done, need review.
- Legal: confirm data handling line items for private deploy customers; asked Eve last week, no reply. Follow-up required.
- UX: quick review of error responses in streaming mode — ask Sophie for 10m after 11.

Launch checklist (canary) — shortlist for tomorrow
- [ ] Canary route configured (10% of internal beta orgs)
- [ ] Autoscaling policy validated under synthetic traffic (throughput & latency)
- [ ] KV cache warmup strategy tested (prefix-heavy workload)
- [ ] Observability: dashboards linked, spike alert + escalation runbook
- [ ] Regression evals: 3 prompt sets run, acceptance pass >= 95% thresholds
- [ ] Rollback plan documented & tested (DB migrations? none)

Notes from 09:00 sync with infra
- Marco: need to add a soft cap on concurrent sessions per org to avoid noisy neighbors; suggested default 1000 sessions — will run perf test later today.
- Infra recommended bumping token-based quotas during rollout window; action: temporary quota increase request to SRE queue.

Risks / open questions
- High-seq workloads still cause p99 spikes on G4-like hardware for >4k tokens. Do we gate large-seq customers from canary? (Pros: reduce risk; Cons: blocks some testers)
- Clear messaging to SDK consumers about fallback model switch (we need a short paragraph for release notes).
- Will support team be staffed for first 48h of canary? Confirm with CS.

Timeboxed tasks for today
- 09:30-10:30: PRD final pass + push to Confluence (blockers inline).
- 11:30-12:00: Stakeholder sync (sales ops + legal quick updates).
- 13:00-14:00: Run regression evals + collect results (Sophie helping).
- 15:00-15:30: Eng sync w/ Marco to finalize autoscale & canary rules.
- 16:00-16:30: Draft release notes + SDK paragraph.

Quick reminders (notes to self)
- Don’t forget to add rollback contact list to runbook (oncall + owners).
- Tag PRD with "locked-for-launch" label after edits.
- Save a copy of final prompts used in evals into shared drive (path: shared_drives/product/hosted-api/evals).

Random scratch ideas (brain dump)
- Could we expose a single-line "cost-estimate" header in the API response for enterprise tenants? Low priority but useful for billing previews.
- Consider adding a lightweight canary monitoring page for non-engineering stakeholders that surfaces only high level metrics.

End-of-day deliverables (what I want closed)
- PRD marked in_review and linked in the launch ticket (PROD-4823).
- Canary config created + smoke test passed.
- Release note draft posted to #prod-launch channel for review.

Unresolved: follow up with Eve (legal) and CS lead (Marta) by noon if no response.

-- Jordan
